title: Base change of the transpose of a unit-valued trace
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale derived categories and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and their constructible exceptional adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\otimes$ for $\otimes_A^L$.

Let $f:V\to S$ be separated finite type and let $b:S'\to S$ be a $k$-morphism. Form $V'=V\times_SS'$ with projections $a:V'\to V$ and $f':V'\to S'$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Put $\omega_f=Rf^!A_S$ and $\omega_{f'}=Rf'^!A_{S'}$. For bounded constructible inputs use the exchange isomorphism $C_M:Lb^*Rf_!M\to Rf'_!La^*M$ of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] and the actual exceptional Hom bijections [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Let $B:La^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ be the transpose of $Lb^*\varepsilon_{f,A_S}\circ C_{\omega_f}^{-1}$, followed by $Lb^*A_S\cong A_{S'}$, with the dualizing base-change convention of [def-pur-co-smoothness].

Let $L\in D^b_c(V,A)$ and $t:Rf_!L\to A_S$, and let $P:L\to\omega_f$ be its adjoint transpose. Suppose $t':Rf'_!La^*L\to A_{S'}$ satisfies $t'\circ C_L=Lb^*t$, with the unit comparison understood. Then its transpose is
$$P'=B\circ La^*P.$$
No smoothness or choice of an identification of either dualizing object with a Tate twist is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $F=Rf_!$, $F'=Rf'_!$, $U=Lb^*$, $V=La^*$ and $u:U A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{S'}$ for the unit comparison. All compositions below are in the stated finite constant-$A$ categories. Use the actual natural Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], restricted to the bounded constructible inputs of the statement as in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. In particular, this uses the constructible adjoints, not an exceptional adjunction on all pro-etale objects. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], the inverse transpose sends $h:M\to Rf^!A_S$ to $\varepsilon_{f,A_S}\circ F(h)$. Abbreviate these counits by $\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon'$. Since $P$ transposes $t$, and $B$ transposes the composite specified in [def-pur-co-smoothness], we have
$$\varepsilon\circ F(P)=t,\qquad \varepsilon'\circ F'(B)=u\circ U(\varepsilon)\circ C_{\omega_f}^{-1}.$$
The same counit characterization holds for the transpose of $t'$ under the $f'$ bijection.

proof.text:
The transformation $C$ is natural in its input. Indeed, [def-cbc-exchange-map] writes compact-support exchange as a composite of the unit, the square isomorphism, the counit, and the extension-by-zero comparison, all natural transformations. Whiskering and composing their naturality squares gives naturality of the composite. The map used here is that exchange transported to the pro-etale etale-origin class, as specified in [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]; composing with the natural comparison isomorphisms still gives a natural transformation. Its components at $L$ and $\omega_f$ are invertible on the domain stipulated in the statement by the same theorem. Apply its naturality square to $P:L\to\omega_f$:
$$C_{\omega_f}\circ U(F(P))=F'(V(P))\circ C_L.$$
Precompose by $C_L^{-1}$ and postcompose by $C_{\omega_f}^{-1}$ to obtain
$$C_{\omega_f}^{-1}\circ F'(V(P))=U(F(P))\circ C_L^{-1}.$$

source.place: Compact-support exchange composite; naturality in the input, applied to P, and then cancellation of the invertible components.

proof.text:
Put $Q=B\circ V(P)$. Using functoriality and the two equations of Step 1, followed by the naturality equation of Step 2, compute its inverse transpose:
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon'\circ F'(Q)
&=\varepsilon'\circ F'(B)\circ F'(V(P))\\
&=u\circ U(\varepsilon)\circ C_{\omega_f}^{-1}\circ F'(V(P))\\
&=u\circ U(\varepsilon)\circ U(F(P))\circ C_L^{-1}\\
&=u\circ U(\varepsilon\circ F(P))\circ C_L^{-1}\\
&=u\circ U(t)\circ C_L^{-1}\\
&=t'.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality follows from the assumed trace equation $t'\circ C_L=u\circ U(t)$ by composition with $C_L^{-1}$. Thus both $Q$ and the transpose $P'$ of $t'$ have inverse transpose $t'$.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), counit formula after the definition; explicit substitution using the exchange naturality square.

proof.text: Apply the injectivity of the inverse Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] for $f'$, source $La^*L$ and target $A_{S'}$. By the counit characterization [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], Step 3 identifies the inverse images of $Q$ and $P'$. Hence $P'=Q=B\circ La^*P$, as claimed. The calculation never inverts $B$ and never uses a Tate identification of either dualizing object.
